welcome_hint: Pick a host in the sidebar, or press the shortcut below to find or connect anywhere.
delete_folder_body: Hosts inside: {hosts}. This cannot be undone.
delete_mode: What to do with the contents
folder_defaults_note: Hosts in this folder use these values unless they set their own.
vault_welcome_hint: Passwords and keys are encrypted on this device. Choose how to unlock them.
vault_mode_keychain_hint: Unlocks automatically with your account. Recommended.
vault_mode_password_hint: Asked on every launch. Cannot be recovered if lost.
err_not_found: Not found. It may have been deleted.
err_cycle: A folder cannot be moved into itself.
err_too_deep: Folders can be nested up to 8 levels.
term_hk_body: {host}:{port} presented a key this app hasn’t seen. Check the fingerprint against one you trust before continuing.
term_hkc_body: The key presented by {host}:{port} doesn’t match the saved one. Someone may be intercepting this connection, or the server was reinstalled. The connection is blocked.
term_hkc_hint: If you trust the change, remove the saved key in Known servers and connect again.
term_link_body: The terminal asked to open this address in your browser.
term_paste_body: Text with several lines can run commands as soon as it lands.
sftp_delete_body_dirs: Folders are deleted with everything inside ({folders}). This cannot be undone.
sftp_open_remote_hint: Open a temporary copy in the default app. Changes stay on this computer.
sftp_open_local_hint: Open this file in the default app.
sftp_open_unsupported: This file type or size cannot be opened here. You can copy the file using the transfer queue.
sftp_open_failed: Could not open the file. Check that an app is associated with this format.
sftp_preview_unsupported: Preview unavailable for this file format or encoding.
sftp_no_host: Open SFTP from a saved host
settings_update_note: Reads the public GitHub releases page. Nothing about you is sent.
password_saved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
host_name_hint: Optional — the address is used if empty
sftp_resize_col: Drag to resize · double-click to reset
stat_unsupported: This server can't report metrics (Linux only).
stat_no_session: Metrics appear once the terminal is connected.
dash_empty_hint: Add your first server to keep availability, metrics and connections in one place.
dash_port_hint: SSH port reachability. Connect to see live metrics.
dash_metrics_hint: Connect to see CPU, memory and network activity.
dash_offline_hint: SSH port is not responding. You can still edit or try connecting.
dash_checked_note: SSH port availability · live metrics for connected servers
snip_vars_hint: {a} asks for a value before running, {b} fills in a default. Each line runs as its own command.
snip_empty_hint: Save the commands you type often and run them with one click on any server, or on several at once.
snip_insert: Paste into the terminal without running
stat_connecting: Connecting; metrics appear right after sign-in…
settings_probe_note: Every 3 minutes opens a TCP connection to the SSH port of servers on the Overview, without signing in. Servers log it as a dropped connection; turn off if you run strict fail2ban.
net_no_ss: The server did not report connections (no ss utility).
net_since: Speed appears in 15 s; until then, bytes since the connections opened
net_udp_note: Ports the server listens on. Whether a firewall blocks them is not visible from here. The kernel does not count UDP per address, so only the port is shown.
stat_last_hint: Not connected. Showing the last sample from {time}.
stat_watch_hint: The server connects in the background after unlock so its metrics are there right away
map_geo_hint: Look up each server's city from its IP address via ipapi.is (ipinfo.io if that has no answer). Only server IP addresses are sent; results stay on this device.
settings_tray_note: A summary of open servers and those that connect at start: state, CPU, memory. Clicking opens the server's Status. After locking, no server names stay in the menu.
dk_missing: Docker is not installed on the server
dk_denied: No access to Docker: log in as root or add the user to the docker group
dk_down: Docker is installed but the service is not running
dk_confirm_body: The container stops answering until it is back up. Open connections to it will drop.
dk_compose_none: No Compose projects. Containers started with docker compose show up here.
dk_events_none: No events in the last hour
ssl_none: No certificates found. Looking at Let's Encrypt, nginx, Apache, Caddy and /root/cert.
ssl_denied: Some certificate folders are closed: log in as root to see all
ssl_no_openssl: No openssl on the server — expiry can't be read
fleet_need_connect: Connect to servers — data from all open ones shows up here at once.
fleet_ssl_denied: Root is needed to see every certificate: {names}
fleet_snip_hint: Commands for any server. Running asks where to send them.
vault_open_failed_hint: The key is kept in the system keychain. If the system asks for permission, choose Always Allow and try again.
vault_legacy_hint: Enter your old master password one last time. After that the app opens by itself and the encryption key stays in this computer's keychain.
settings_keychain_note: Your data is encrypted; the key is kept in this computer's keychain. The app opens without a password.
cx_waiting: waiting for a reply · {n} s of {max}
cx_d_dns_h: The server name did not turn into an IP address. Check how it is written in the server settings, and that you are online.
cx_d_dns_timeout_h: The address was not found within 15 s. You may be offline, or the DNS server is not answering.
cx_d_refused_h: Nothing is listening at {addr}. SSH may not be running, or the server settings have the wrong port.
cx_d_unreachable_h: The network does not know how to reach {addr}. Check your internet connection and the server address.
cx_d_tcp_timeout_h: No reply from {addr} within 15 s. The server may be off, the port blocked by a firewall, or there is no connectivity.
cx_d_jump_t: The jump host could not reach the server
cx_d_jump_h: The previous server in the chain is reachable but could not open a connection onward. Check that the next host is reachable from it.
cx_d_hs_timeout_h: The port is open, but SSH did not answer within 30 s. Another service may be on that port, or connection protection is active.
cx_d_hs_dropped_h: The port is open, but the server closed the connection before sign-in. This happens with brute-force protection (fail2ban), connection limits or IP filters.
cx_d_hs_algo_h: The server and the app found no shared method ({detail}). The server may be too old or configured very strictly.
cx_d_hs_protocol_t: The server did not speak SSH
cx_d_hs_protocol_h: It looks like something other than SSH runs on this port. Check the port in the server settings.
cx_d_auth_t: The server did not accept the sign-in
cx_d_auth_h: The server accepts: {methods}. Check the username and the password or key in the server settings.
cx_d_auth_none_h: The server offers no more ways to sign in. Check the username and the password or key in the server settings.
cx_d_channel_t: Signed in, but the terminal did not open
cx_d_channel_h: The server accepted you but would not open a shell. It may limit the number of sessions, or shells may be disabled.
cx_d_no_user_h: Open the server settings and enter a user.
cx_d_no_host_h: Open the server settings and enter the address.
cx_d_prepare_h: The app could not gather the data it needs to connect.
term_end_shell_exited: the session ended on the server
term_end_keepalive: the server stopped answering keep-alive checks
term_end_inactivity: the connection was closed for inactivity
term_end_server_TooManyConnections: the server closed the connection: too many connections
term_end_server_ConnectionLost: the server reported a lost connection
backup_note: One encrypted file: servers and folders, passwords and keys, snippets, trusted server keys and all settings. On another computer open Restore here and everything is back.
backup_pw_hint: At least {min} characters. Without it the file cannot be opened, and a forgotten password cannot be recovered.
backup_restore_note: Servers from the file are added to the current ones; what is already here stays. Settings from the file replace the current ones.
backup_restored: Restored: {hosts} servers, {folders} folders, {identities} keys and passwords, {snippets} snippets, {settings} settings.
fleet_need_connect_hint: Connect to servers and data from all open ones shows up here.
tabs_background_hint: Connected for monitoring without taking tabs. They are on Overview; open a server and it joins the tabs.
snip_folder_exists: A folder with this name already exists
snip_folder_delete_body: Snippets are kept: {count} will move to “No folder”.
snip_folder_delete_empty: The folder is empty; nothing else changes.
close_ask_body: The server is connected. Keep it in the background so monitoring in Overview keeps running.
close_ask_keep_hint: The tab closes; the connection and monitoring continue
close_ask_disconnect_hint: Close the tab and drop the connection
notes_placeholder: What the server is for, who owns it, what to remember…
keys_hint: Press ? anywhere to open this window.
keys_sidebar: Show or hide the server list
start_server_hint: Address, user and sign-in method. Everything stays on this computer.
start_key_hint: An SSH key file, if you do not sign in with a password. You can also pick one later, in the server card.
start_backup_hint: An encrypted file with all servers and keys: handy if you ever have to reinstall your system.
settings_term_theme_note: To give one server or folder its own theme, open its editor and look under Advanced.
settings_keys_note: Everything saved for signing in to servers. You add them in a server's editor.
key_confirm_used: Delete “{name}”? Servers and folders using it: {count}. They will lose this sign-in.
settings_known_note: Keys of the servers you trusted. If a server was reinstalled, delete its entry and connect again: the app will show the new key for review.
settings_known_capped: Showing the first {count}. Narrow the search.
host_window_wait_connection: Wait for the connection to finish before moving the tab.
term_drop_started: Uploading to {dir}, files: {count}. Progress is in Files
settings_notify: Tell me when a background command finishes
settings_notify_note: When you are in another tab or app and the terminal shows its prompt again (or rings the bell), you get a notification. It is guessed from the output, so it can occasionally miss.
fwd_empty: Open a server port on this computer, a port of this computer on the server, or a SOCKS5 proxy through the server.
fwd_hint_local: A service of the server or its network opens here. For example, a database on the server becomes localhost:5432.
fwd_hint_remote: A port of this computer opens on the server. For example, to show the server something running here.
fwd_hint_dynamic: A proxy on this computer: a browser or app goes online through the server.
fwd_exposed: Address {addr} opens the port to other devices on the network. Keep 127.0.0.1 for this computer only.
fwd_need_session: Connect to the server to start it
fwd_err_dest: Enter the destination host and port (1–65535)
imp_not_found: ~/.ssh/config was not found. If you use ssh in a terminal, your hosts are usually listed there.
imp_empty: ~/.ssh/config has no hosts with concrete names.
imp_key_encrypted: passphrase-protected key is not copied; sign-in goes through ssh-agent
keygen_rsa_note: RSA 4096 is only for old servers that do not support Ed25519.
keygen_done: Key created. Copy its public part with the button next to it.
settings_keys_note2: Everything saved for signing in to servers. Create a key here or on a server page, where you can also install it.
keylogin_now_password: Signs in with a password now. A key is safer and you will not need the password.
keylogin_now_none: No key chosen for this server.
keylogin_run: Install and sign in with key
keylogin_need_session: Connect to the server to install the key
keylogin_done: Key installed. The next sign-in uses the key.
keylogin_already: The key was already on the server. The next sign-in uses the key.
keylogin_note: The public part of the key is added to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server. The password stays saved.
startup_tmux: tmux: resume the session after a drop
startup_tmux_note: Attaches to the tmux session “main” or creates it. After a dropped connection you are back where you were. tmux must be installed on the server.
settings_auto_reconnect_note: When the network drops, the computer wakes up or the server reboots, the app tries again: after 1, 2, 4… up to 30 seconds, and right after the network is back. With tmux (host editor, “Startup command”) you return to the same session.
